Attio.notes: API access requires an active Attio workspace; the documentation does not specify whether the workspace can be created for free or requires a paid plan.

Zendesk.description: Zendesk is a support/helpdesk platform. The provided text focuses on community MCP servers that wrap Zendesk's API. It confirms Zendesk exposes a public API supporting Help Center article search/create/update/translate, and Support ticket management (create, view, update, comments, triage, attachments). Authentication is via OAuth (openid and offline_access scopes). No API keys are used. Access may require enabling custom apps by an administrator.

Slack.description: Slack offers a public MCP server enabling integrated apps to search channels, send/retrieve messages, manage canvases, users, files, and lists via MCP clients. Workspace admins can approve and manage MCP client integrations. The MCP server provides tools for searching messages/files/users/channels/emoji, sending and reading messages, creating conversations, adding reactions, managing canvases, fetching user info, uploading files (two-step), and working with structured lists.
Slack.mcp_notes: Official Slack MCP server documented at https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server. Provides tools for search, messaging, canvases, users, files, and lists. Workspace admins can approve/manage MCP client integrations.
blockers: Workspace admin approval required for MCP client integrations
Slack.notes: The scraped text focuses on the MCP server. It mentions "on behalf of the authenticated user" implying OAuth2, and Slack's well-known API uses OAuth2 and API keys (bot tokens). The text does not explicitly name auth methods, so auth_methods is inferred from Slack's standard model. Access model is free_signup based on Slack's standard free workspace offering. Admin approval for MCP integrations is a soft blocker but not a hard one for self-serve developers.

API keys can be created by users with Owner, Admin, or Manager roles.

Media must be hosted on a public server for publishing.

Shopify.description: Shopify's Customer Accounts MCP server provides tools for customer-specific actions (order management, account details) for AI assistants. It uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE, with the MCP endpoint dynamically discovered from the shop's storefront domain.
Shopify.mcp_notes: Shopify publishes official MCP servers: Customer Accounts MCP server (https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/storefront-mcp/servers/customer-account) and an Order MCP server (https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/orders/order-mcp).

Shopify.notes: Access to the Customer Accounts MCP server is gated: requires a custom domain, meeting protected customer data requirements, completing integration steps, and requesting Level 2 protected customer data (PII) access from the Shopify Partner dashboard. So while Shopify has a self-serve developer platform, this specific MCP server has approval/PII-access prerequisites.

Ahrefs.description: Ahrefs API v3 provides programmatic access to SEO, marketing, and AI-search data (backlinks, traffic, keywords, SERPs, rank tracking, site audits, brand/AI visibility, web/social analytics, account management). Organized into tools, each a group of REST endpoints with full OpenAPI specs. Base URL https://api.ahrefs.com/v3/{tool}/{endpoint}. Auth via API key as Bearer token; free 'public' endpoints need no key. GET requests, JSON/XML responses, select/where parameters, API-unit-based billing.
Ahrefs.mcp_notes: MCP server for Ahrefs referenced at apis.io/apis/ahrefs/mcp/ and a setup guide at studiomeyer.io/en/blog/ahrefs-mcp-server-setup.
blockers: Most billable endpoints require an Ahrefs subscription and consume API units
Ahrefs.notes: API access appears tied to an Ahrefs subscription for most billable endpoints (API units), but free 'public' endpoints and free test queries exist and a free/public APIv3 key can be created. Self-serve key creation is documented.

Firecrawl.description: Firecrawl MCP server exposes a REST API for searching, scraping, parsing, and monitoring web content. It supports keyless access with daily limits, OAuth2 account sign‑in, or an API key as bearer token. The API is documented on the Firecrawl docs site and can be used immediately by developers.
Firecrawl.mcp_notes: Official MCP server: https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (OAuth endpoint: https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth)
Firecrawl.notes: Keyless mode provides limited daily usage; full access requires an API key or OAuth sign‑in.

Linear.description: Linear's MCP server provides a standardized interface for AI models/agents to access Linear data (issues, projects, comments). It uses Streamable HTTP transport at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp, with OAuth 2.1 (dynamic client registration) as the primary auth, plus bearer token or Linear API key options. Read-write and read-only endpoints are available.
Linear.mcp_notes: Official Linear MCP server at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (read-write) and https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly (read-only). Centrally hosted, follows authenticated remote MCP spec. Setup pages for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Codex, Jules.
Linear.notes: Text focuses on the MCP server, not the broader REST API, but the MCP exposes tools for finding/creating/updating issues, projects, and comments. Auth is OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, or a Linear API key (generated in Settings > Account > Security & Access). Enterprise orgs can use Okta SAML-managed auth. No blockers for self-serve access.
